messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Joint Hyperparameter Fitting and Predictive Inference
parts:
(Thought I sent this yesterday, but see now it wasn't)

I found this code:

https://github.com/mclark--/Miscellaneous-R-Code/blob/master/ModelFitting/gp%20Examples/gpStanModelCode.stan

which implements the fitting+prediction using the "Analytical Form of Joint Predictive Inference" approach. 

One thing, however, is that since the noise term sigma_sq is added to the diagonal of both Sigma and Omega, I believe the resulting predictions reflect uncertainty on are for future observed data series y, whereas I'd like to reflect only uncertainty on the underlying wiggly function. This previous stan-users post (https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/wL-O3SSrcAw/iiDcnIGqt9gJ) implies that I merely need omit addition of sigma_sq to the diagonal of Omega to achieve this, however when I do so I get an error immediately upon sampling saying "Error : Exception thrown at line 104: cholesky_decompose: Cholesky decomposition of m failed". Any idea what's gone awry and how to implement the uncertainty-on-f predictions?

Thanks in advance,

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~
